title: Xanthe and the Inheritance
premise: Quentin Villalobos, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after the funeral of the cathedral's late benefactor — a letter claiming the man's death was witnessed by someone everyone swears drowned thirty years ago. Following the letter's clues through the locked crypt and the tidal flats beneath it, Quentin discovers the 'dead' witness is alive, hidden in plain sight as the benefactor's devoted housekeeper, and that the inheritance being contested is a cover for a decades-old crime. In the end, Quentin must choose between closing the case cleanly for the diocese and protecting the found family the witness has built; she chooses the truth, but delivers it on her own terms, letting the tide return what it took.
about_author: Ines Fairweather is a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing wills, letters, and lies in English coastal towns. She writes mysteries about the secrets institutions keep and the people who keep them anyway.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A confession letter arrives addressed to her personally, postmarked the day after Archibald Crane's funeral, naming a witness who died thirty years ago. She files it, then can't sleep. Emotional beat: the itch of an unclosable case.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Quentin surveys the sealed crypt Crane endowed, finding his recent fingerprints on a door locked since 1994. POV: Quentin. Beat: dread mixed with professional delight — the case has teeth.

chapters.title: Mourners and Liars
chapters.summary: At the wake, Quentin interviews the family: the bitter nephew Desmond, the grieving widow Edith, and the quiet housekeeper Maren Hale. Each alibi is polished. POV: Quentin. Beat: unease beneath civility.

chapters.title: A Witness, Drowned
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter via the 1994 inquest file: Tomas Reyes fell from the tidal causeway; his body was never recovered. POV: alternating Quentin reading documents with brief Reyes-voice excerpts. Beat: the past pressing upward.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Quentin walks the causeway at low tide, finds a modern padlock rusted into the old sea wall — someone has been going down there recently. POV: Quentin. Beat: cold certainty that the dead are walking.

chapters.title: Desmond's Claim
chapters.summary: Desmond pressures the diocese to open the crypt before probate, hinting Quentin's job depends on cooperation. POV: Quentin. Beat: duty tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Edith's Grief
chapters.summary: Edith reveals Crane spent his last weeks writing letters he burned, weeping over a name. POV: Edith. Beat: tenderness and misdirection — grief that knows more than it says.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Keys
chapters.summary: Quentin notices Maren's keyring holds a key worn to match the crypt lock. Maren deflects with perfect calm. POV: Quentin. Beat: suspicion curdling into reluctant respect.

chapters.title: Second Letter
chapters.summary: Another letter arrives — this one written in a living hand, warning Quentin to stop. Postmark: tomorrow's date. POV: Quentin. Beat: fear; the case is watching her back.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Quentin's own circle — the verger, the fishmonger, her estranged sister — pull closer as she isolates herself. POV: Quentin with sister-call interlude. Beat: warmth against obsession; theme of found family mirrored.

chapters.title: Down Below
chapters.summary: Quentin picks the crypt lock at night and finds a cot, a lamp, fresh bread crumbs — someone lives below the cathedral. POV: Quentin. Beat: vertigo; the mystery becomes flesh.

chapters.title: Tomas Reyes, Alive
chapters.summary: She confronts the inhabitant: Tomas Reyes, disfigured by the fall, hiding for thirty years because he saw who killed the man whose money built everything. POV: Tomas. Beat: relief and terror entwined.

chapters.title: The Confession He Wrote
chapters.summary: Tomas explains: Crane was dying and wanted to confess publicly; the letters were meant to clear Tomas's name. Someone intercepted them. POV: Tomas. Beat: hope rekindled, then shadowed — who mailed the first letter?

chapters.title: Maren's Silence
chapters.summary: Quentin realizes Maren has been feeding and shielding Tomas for years — the housekeeper is his daughter. POV: Maren. Beat: love against duty; she chose her father over the law.

chapters.title: Desmond Knows
chapters.summary: Desmond confronts Quentin, revealing he found the crypt years ago and has been blackmailing Maren to control the inheritance. POV: Quentin. Beat: the villain steps out of the margins.

chapters.title: The Night of the Funeral
chapters.summary: Reconstruction: Desmond intercepted Crane's final letter, mailed it late to frame the timing, and plans to seal Tomas below permanently once probate clears. POV: Desmond. Beat: chilling banality of greed.

chapters.title: Trapped Below
chapters.summary: Desmond locks Quentin in the crypt as the tide rises; water seeps through the old sea wall. POV: Quentin. Beat: primal fear; the tide giving up what it took — or taking her.

chapters.title: The Causeway Choice
chapters.summary: Maren, torn between silence and saving Quentin, opens the crypt from outside and pulls her out as the tide turns. POV: Maren. Beat: duty broken by love; the found family completes itself.

chapters.title: Everything the Light Touches
chapters.summary: Quentin lays the full case before the diocese: blackmail, the false inquest, Tomas's survival. Desmond flees toward the causeway. POV: Quentin. Beat: resolve hardening into action.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: On the flats, Desmond slips on the same rocks that broke Tomas; Quentin saves him anyway, choosing the person over the punishment. POV: Quentin. Beat: mercy as climax — love against duty resolved.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Probate court: Crane's true will surfaces from the crypt wall, leaving everything to Tomas and Maren; the diocese quietly closes the crypt forever. POV: Quentin. Beat: justice without spectacle.

chapters.title: A Case Closed, A Door Opened
chapters.summary: Quentin archives the letters under her own name, visits Tomas and Maren for Sunday supper, and finally sleeps. POV: Quentin. Beat: peace; identity chosen, family found, the tide at rest.
